questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Namondo wants to purchase a printer for her office computer to print **hard copies** of her photographs. She wants to know which printer type is cheaper: **Impact** or **non-impact**. She is advised that although impact printers are cheaper, the most important things to consider in buying a printer are **print quality**, and the **cost and rate of consumption of ink**.

(i) Which printer is she likely to select? Justify your answer. (3 marks)

(ii) What do you understand by the terms?

- Hard copy
- Impact printer
- Non-impact printer
- Print quality

(6 marks)

(iii) State a difference between impact and non-impact printer in terms of their print technology. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Choice of printer (3 marks).** Namondo is likely to select a **non-impact printer** (an inkjet or a laser printer). Justification: she wants to print photographs, which need a high print quality (fine detail, smooth colours, good resolution). Impact printers (such as the dot-matrix printer) are cheaper, but their print quality is poor and they cannot reproduce photographs. Since print quality is the most important criterion, the extra cost of a non-impact printer (and of its ink or toner) is justified.

**(ii) Terms (6 marks, 1.5 marks each)**

- **Hard copy:** a permanent printed copy of a document or image, produced on paper by a printer.
- **Impact printer:** a printer that forms characters or dots by physically striking an inked ribbon against the paper (for example dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers).
- **Non-impact printer:** a printer that prints without striking the paper, for example by spraying tiny drops of ink (inkjet) or by using a laser, toner and heat (laser printer).
- **Print quality:** how sharp, clear and detailed the printed output is; it depends on the resolution (dots per inch) and the number of colours that the printer can produce.

**(iii) Difference in print technology (2 marks).** An impact printer prints by mechanical contact: pins or hammers hit an inked ribbon against the paper. A non-impact printer has no striking mechanism: it sprays ink droplets onto the paper (inkjet) or transfers toner with a laser, static electricity and heat (laser). As a result impact printers are noisy and non-impact printers are quiet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Consider the logic circuit diagram in Figure 1 below:

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

(i) State the names of the logic gates labelled A, B and C. (3 marks)

(ii) Based on Figure 1, copy and complete the truth table in Figure 2. (3 marks)

| X | Y | P | Q | R |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |   |   |   |
| 0 | 1 |   |   |   |
| 1 | 0 |   |   |   |
| 1 | 1 |   |   |   |

Figure 2

(iii) Write the logic equations for outputs **P**, **Q** and **R** in terms of X and Y. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading Figure 1.** Gate A (curved back, pointed front) has the inputs X and Y and gives P. Gate B (flat back) also has the inputs X and Y and gives Q. Gate C (flat back with a small circle at the output) has the inputs P and Q and gives R.

**(i) Names of the gates (3 marks).**

- A is an **OR** gate;
- B is an **AND** gate;
- C is a **NAND** gate (an AND gate followed by a NOT; the small circle is the inversion).

**(ii) Completed truth table (3 marks).** $P = X \text{ OR } Y$, $Q = X \text{ AND } Y$ and $R = \text{NOT}(P \text{ AND } Q)$.

| X | Y | P | Q | R |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

For example, for X = 1 and Y = 0: P = 1 OR 0 = 1, Q = 1 AND 0 = 0, so R = NOT(1 AND 0) = NOT(0) = 1.

**(iii) Logic equations (3 marks).**

$$P = X + Y \qquad (X \text{ OR } Y)$$

$$Q = X \cdot Y \qquad (X \text{ AND } Y)$$

$$R = \overline{P \cdot Q} \qquad (P \text{ NAND } Q)$$

Substituting, $R = \overline{(X + Y)\cdot(X \cdot Y)} = \overline{X \cdot Y}$, so the whole circuit behaves as a NAND gate of X and Y (the last column of the table is 1, 1, 1, 0).
